jobs.title: Grant Writer
jobs.description:
Company Description
Night Sky Rescue Inc. is a mission-driven nonprofit organization based in Santa Barbara, CA, dedicated to protecting and preserving wildlife and natural habitats. The organization focuses on rescue, rehabilitation, and conservation efforts, working closely with community partners, volunteers, and local agencies. Night Sky Rescue Inc. values collaboration, transparency, and measurable impact in all of its programs and initiatives. Team members are encouraged to bring forward ideas, contribute to strategic growth, and support fundraising activities that sustain long-term conservation efforts. The organization offers a supportive environment for individuals passionate about environmental stewardship and community engagement.
Role Description
This is a full-time, on-site Grant Writer role located in Santa Barbara, CA. The Grant Writer is responsible for identifying and researching potential grant opportunities from foundations, corporations, and government agencies aligned with Night Sky Rescue Inc.’s mission. Day-to-day tasks include drafting compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and reports; collecting and organizing data and program information; and collaborating with program staff to accurately represent project goals, outcomes, and budgets. The role involves managing a grant calendar, tracking submission deadlines and reporting requirements, and maintaining accurate records of proposals, awards, and donor communications. The Grant Writer will also contribute to the development of fundraising materials and support broader development initiatives as needed.
Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in professional writing, particularly in grant writing or fundraising proposals, with strong skills in clarity, organization, and concise storytelling.
Ability to conduct thorough research on funding opportunities, analyze grant guidelines, and align organizational programs with funder priorities.
Competence in basic budgeting concepts and ability to collaborate with finance or program teams to develop accurate grant budgets and narratives.
Strong organizational and time-management skills, including managing multiple deadlines, maintaining detailed records, and prioritizing tasks effectively.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor messaging to diverse audiences such as funders, partners, and internal stakeholders.
Proficiency with standard office and productivity software (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, presentations) and familiarity with donor or grants management systems is beneficial.
Experience working in or with nonprofit organizations, especially in environmental, wildlife, or conservation fields, is a plus.
Bachelor’s degree in Communications, English, Nonprofit Management, Environmental Studies, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Commitment to the mission of Night Sky Rescue Inc., with a collaborative mindset and ability to work effectively as part of an on-site team.

The Children and Families Department takes a strengths-based approach to working with each other, children, young people and families, and our partner agencies. We call this 'Our Nottinghamshire Approach'. Watch the two minute animation to learn more.

Join Nottinghamshire County Council
, a dedicated team committed to making a difference in the lives of children and families. We believe in creating a supportive environment where everyone can thrive. Our Bassetlaw Family Support & Safeguarding Team is a vibrant mix of professionals working together to provide essential services to our community.

We have an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and knowledgeable Family Support Worker
to join our dynamic team. You will play a vital role in working with children, families, and professionals to achieve positive outcomes. If you have a passion for childcare and a drive to make a difference, this role is for you!

As a Family Support Worker, your key responsibilities will include:

Collaborating with children, families, and professionals to develop tailored support plans.
Engaging with families to provide guidance and support in achieving their goals.
Maintaining accurate records and documentation of your work.
Participating in team meetings and contributing to a positive team environment.
Delivering structured interventions and support to families in need.

To Succeed In This Role, You Will Need

Experience working with children and families, ideally in a social care setting.
A thorough understanding of safeguarding and child protection issues.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively.

We Are Looking For Candidates Who Demonstrate

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
A warm and caring personality, with the ability to build positive relationships.
A commitment to working collaboratively within a multi-disciplinary team.
A proactive approach to problem-solving and decision-making.

At Nottinghamshire County Council, We Offer

A place to belong: a friendly, inclusive workplace where everyone is valued.
Opportunities for professional development and training to help you grow in your career.
Regular supervision and support to ensure your success.
A commitment to work-life balance, with flexible working options available.

Don’t miss out on this opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of families in our community! If you are passionate about supporting children and families, we want to hear from you. Apply today and be part of a team that truly cares!

For an informal discussion about this opportunity please contact Melanie Wass
on 0115 8042954
or by email melanie.wass1@nottscc.gov.uk.

This post is also available as a secondment opportunity to existing Nottinghamshire County Council employees. You must seek approval from your line manager before applying.

Appointment to this post is subject to a Disclosure and Barring Service check.

Nottinghamshire County Council strives to ensure that it goes beyond the requirements of the Equalities Act and prides itself on being accredited as a Disability Confident Leader Organisation.

Under the Disability Confident scheme (formerly known as the Guaranteed Interview Scheme) we would like to ensure applicants with disabilities are offered an interview if they meet the minimum criteria for a job. Please let us know if this is something you would like to be considered for.

A job share scheme is available for all full-time posts: both permanent and temporary, unless otherwise stated.

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and we expect all staff to share this commitment and undergo appropriate checks.

Nottinghamshire County Council strongly encourages applications from all candidates from different walks of life, irrespective of gender, marital status, disability, race, religion, belief, pregnancy and maternity status, age or sexual orientation.
